head.text: PROPOSED (changes.md CS2): IDE register write, base window (PIO mode 0), 10-clock cycle

signal.name: state
signal.data: S0 S1 S2 Sw Sw Sw Sw Sw Sw Sw Sw Sw Sw Sw Sw Sw Sw S3 S4 S5 S0 S1

foot.text: Proposed. Drawn at 16 MHz (1 slot = 15.6 ns). nIDE_WR is a falling-edge register fed by the counter, so it cannot glitch: low from edge 2 to edge 7, 312 ns. The drive latches the data on the rising edge of /IOW, two clocks before AS negates, with /CS0 and the data still valid (t9 113 ns and t4 116 ns at 16 MHz). nIDE_RD_INH stays high in write cycles, so nCPU_RD never asserts. IDE2 uses the same strobe; only the selects differ. A fast-window write has /IOW from edge 1 to edge 3 and a 5-clock cycle.
